name: Sepu Badi
ingredients: Whole spices (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf)
instructions: 1. Soak the dals overnight, grind them into a smooth paste, and mix with chopped spinach and salt.
2. Steam the batter in a greased container until firm, then cut into small squares (badi).
3. Deep-fry the badi until golden brown and keep aside.
4. Prepare the gravy by sautéing ginger-garlic paste and onions in mustard oil, followed by adding the dry spices.
5. Whisk the yogurt and add it to the pan, stirring continuously to prevent curdling.
6. Add the fried badi to the gravy and simmer on low heat until the dumplings absorb the flavors.
description: Sepu Badi is a royal delicacy from the Mandi district of Himachal Pradesh. Traditionally served at Dham (community feasts), it is a labor-intensive dish known for its unique texture and the rich, tangy yogurt gravy that defines Himachali celebratory cuisine.
